title: How to turn a YouTube playlist into a course
description: Turn any YouTube playlist into a structured course: split it into lessons, add a daily plan, check what you learn, and keep the videos in YouTube's player. By hand, or in a minute with CourseIt.
answer: To turn a YouTube playlist into a course, split the videos into short lessons, schedule them into days around a daily time budget, and add a few questions after each lesson. CourseIt does this from the playlist link.
body:
## What a course has that a playlist doesn't

A playlist is a list of videos. A course adds four things on top: **lessons** sized to one sitting, a **schedule** with a finish line, a way to **check you understood**, and a way to **skip what you already know**. You can add all four yourself, and the videos can stay exactly where they are.

## Doing it by hand

### 1. List the videos and their lengths

Open the playlist and write down each video with its length. This is your raw material, and adding up the lengths tells you how big the course really is.

### 2. Cut long videos into lessons

Use the creator's chapters where they exist: they're the timestamps in the video description and the sections on the progress bar. Where there are none, skim and note where the topic changes. Aim for lessons short enough to finish in one sitting, and write each one down as "video, start time, end time, topic".

### 3. Pack the lessons into days

Pick the minutes you can give it on a normal day. Go down your lesson list and fill each day up to that budget without splitting a lesson. Now you have a finish date.

### 4. Write questions for each lesson

After watching a lesson, write two or three questions it should let you answer. Answer them from memory the next day before moving on. If you can't, rewatch that part.

### 5. Test out of the early lessons

If the playlist starts with material you know, try the questions for those lessons first. Drop the ones you can answer and keep the rest.

This works, but it takes a while for a long playlist, and the hard part is still showing up each day: see [how to finish a YouTube course](/guides/how-to-finish-a-youtube-course) for that.

## Doing it with CourseIt

Paste the playlist (or a single video) link into [CourseIt](/). It reads each video's own captions and builds the course for you:

- **Lessons** split on topic boundaries, snapped to the creator's chapters when there are any.
- **Study notes** and a short **quiz** for every lesson, with a "Replay the moment" button that jumps the video back to where a missed idea is taught.
- A **placement test** that drops the lessons you already know from your plan.
- A **daily plan** packed around the minutes a day you choose, which updates when you change your pace.

Videos play in YouTube's own player, so the creator keeps the view. A few limits worth knowing: a course is built from captions, so videos without captions are left out, and a playlist can have up to 200 videos and 20 hours of video, within your plan's limits (see [pricing](/pricing)).

Someone may already have built the playlist you want. Check the [course library](/library) first: joining a course someone else built is always free.
